#harmony #songwriting

Progressions I keep reaching for on sessions and in my own songs, with where I nicked them from. Roman numerals because I play in whatever key the singer says on the day.

## I - V - vi - IV

The four chords of every pop song since 1985. Not ashamed. Kirsty's "Saltcoats" is this in A at 104 BPM. Trick to stop it sounding like a busking pitch on Buchanan Street: start on the vi instead (vi - IV - I - V), and the whole song suddenly feels sadder.

## ii - V - I

Jazz bread and butter. On the ES-335 I play it with the shell voicings Morag drilled into me on piano: root, 3rd, 7th only. In C: Dm7 - G7 - Cmaj7. Add the 9th on the Dm7 and the 13th on the G7 when the bass player is competent. Practising round the cycle of fourths, see [[Guitar practice]].

## The backdoor ii - V

iv7 - bVII7 - I. In C: Fm7 - Bb7 - C. Sounds like an old Hollywood ending, which is why I like it. Used it as the outro on a demo for the Rankine Family Band in July 2024 and the fiddle player asked what witchcraft that was.

## Andalusian cadence

i - bVII - bVI - V. Am - G - F - E. Every flamenco student meets this on day one, see [[Flamenco compás]]. It's also "Hit the Road Jack" and half of every spaghetti western score. The E major at the end is the bit that matters, it should almost hurt.

## Modal vamps

Two-chord vamps that sit in one mode:

- Dorian: Am7 - D7 (the D major chord is the Dorian giveaway, F#). "Oye Como Va" territory.
- Mixolydian: G - F - C - G. Every Scottish folk rock band ever, mine included.
- Lydian: C - D/C. Film music shorthand for wonder.

More on the scales behind these in [[Music theory modes]].

## Chromatic mediants

C major to E major or Ab major, no pivot. John Williams lives here. I used C - Ab - C under a pad for the Strathbungo Film Society intro sting in 2023 and it worked better than it had any right to.

## Line clichés

Hold the chord, move one inner voice down by semitones. Am - Am(maj7) - Am7 - Am6. James Bond, "Michelle", "Stairway". On guitar, the moving voice goes on the G string.

## Songs I'm writing, and what's under them

- "Clydebank Rain" (working title): vi - IV - I - V in D, capo 2, 88 BPM.
- "Night Bus to Paisley": backdoor ii - V turnaround every 8 bars, 72 BPM, 12/8 feel.
- Instrumental for the film club's horror night: Andalusian cadence played on a detuned synth, see [[Synth patch notes]].

## Rule of thumb

If a progression sounds clever, the melody probably needs to be simpler. If the melody is clever, play the four chords. I've broken this rule on every demo I've hated.
